To get rid of alcohol bloating quickly, ` [Highlight start] drink plenty of water and electrolytes, avoid more alcohol and salty or carbonated foods, and take a gentle walk to help your digestive tract move gas and fluid [Highlight end] ` . Most mild bloating from drinking clears up within 24 to 72 hours.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXjBiVYQK0-L7SfHRFtvJo0XYEKHN5ToRsxJEsgNCt0ksS944EVYxiJsdIYE70aWzNstk5NRRcQAzUDxkqpQffgWZ-zGgkregGHMTcDIlpObtOQ53HQdOuML_TJDZ8l18SwdlWEdeqQo8Qdvb9llDw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF1zDRvHoBHQnZcjOQy3wh0z1mLCsks0rJeOFrAi4YnMm6jgunxp_XBQQQXaDmHQeBB-X9n85vM932Y3HLOcKbbNwXHkgiWLN00S0PWpbWYTJUM9mkH94BIkWA1LU2LkG7-q31pGOYComi4BzOmi81Cr8Dhwie19fZOC9VLdHyEjS0sAHd)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1_HEBAcI_T82Vm7Fe3U8nltvZiJhs3JX0ARhoorNGW5O5wQ7yNUwdQ4yHl41pt5C9dL0auli7euA_cjDt7O_v5ylsVTZ3AsKIKCv8cfjtfMMmHt0-tS5GDzyKcfaoRru_UnUnDGLIbUXIIxP1PT10SsPcH4LCL6Qh3k_D_dUjK0bACqb9fqWdIgCo-s)

### Immediate Relief Steps

- **Rehydrate:** Drink water consistently to help your body release excess fluid it holds onto during dehydration. Electrolytes—like coconut water, electrolyte drinks, or potassium-rich foods (bananas, avocados, spinach)—can help restore fluid balance.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1_HEBAcI_T82Vm7Fe3U8nltvZiJhs3JX0ARhoorNGW5O5wQ7yNUwdQ4yHl41pt5C9dL0auli7euA_cjDt7O_v5ylsVTZ3AsKIKCv8cfjtfMMmHt0-tS5GDzyKcfaoRru_UnUnDGLIbUXIIxP1PT10SsPcH4LCL6Qh3k_D_dUjK0bACqb9fqWdIgCo-s)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEBxCJF15WjJZE00fW0KHTBTHs1HI1oLAoSIMrQ3JN1v-yNBT2ZfmQRJAmc1UUkLCi8LmiHTivD25Cinagvp9ai_cwefZKi5l2PhtyUExKEYNytaW66KXA2uNMkMLTu0VYtovvByHY8szwoOuNx53e84z8d4pnb2BxG9YfrzTiBgsVyJAhsyQtKKG0SspwwlLOHJg)
- **Move gently:** A light 10- to 20-minute walk stimulates digestion and helps relieve trapped gas.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1_HEBAcI_T82Vm7Fe3U8nltvZiJhs3JX0ARhoorNGW5O5wQ7yNUwdQ4yHl41pt5C9dL0auli7euA_cjDt7O_v5ylsVTZ3AsKIKCv8cfjtfMMmHt0-tS5GDzyKcfaoRru_UnUnDGLIbUXIIxP1PT10SsPcH4LCL6Qh3k_D_dUjK0bACqb9fqWdIgCo-s)
- **Soothe your stomach:** Sip warm herbal tea (such as ginger, peppermint, or chamomile) to calm digestive spasms and reduce gas . Applying mild warmth to your abdomen may also ease discomfort.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF1zDRvHoBHQnZcjOQy3wh0z1mLCsks0rJeOFrAi4YnMm6jgunxp_XBQQQXaDmHQeBB-X9n85vM932Y3HLOcKbbNwXHkgiWLN00S0PWpbWYTJUM9mkH94BIkWA1LU2LkG7-q31pGOYComi4BzOmi81Cr8Dhwie19fZOC9VLdHyEjS0sAHd)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXjBiVYQK0-L7SfHRFtvJo0XYEKHN5ToRsxJEsgNCt0ksS944EVYxiJsdIYE70aWzNstk5NRRcQAzUDxkqpQffgWZ-zGgkregGHMTcDIlpObtOQ53HQdOuML_TJDZ8l18SwdlWEdeqQo8Qdvb9llDw)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1_HEBAcI_T82Vm7Fe3U8nltvZiJhs3JX0ARhoorNGW5O5wQ7yNUwdQ4yHl41pt5C9dL0auli7euA_cjDt7O_v5ylsVTZ3AsKIKCv8cfjtfMMmHt0-tS5GDzyKcfaoRru_UnUnDGLIbUXIIxP1PT10SsPcH4LCL6Qh3k_D_dUjK0bACqb9fqWdIgCo-s)
- **Use targeted OTC options if needed:** Over-the-counter antacids or acid reducers can ease acid irritation, while simethicone can help break up trapped gas.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEBxCJF192lTMBxP4_BMx7jI7bzaij4dUDZ9q_BPQ1Zsdncjn6HgynIK8Ci9EH55vz4r2ZXwP3bRzP5gT2hTmyzXgPea9VBJiqfW_YrD_VvBDNqMf74S30mhLl7DmOmi-qj8VP2YhCji2oXuComBxTmoL0d5SMVjDjlrzYy6wioyovSkKF92oLEaKhJCukB-3xRfA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1_HEBAcI_T82Vm7Fe3U8nltvZiJhs3JX0ARhoorNGW5O5wQ7yNUwdQ4yHl41pt5C9dL0auli7euA_cjDt7O_v5ylsVTZ3AsKIKCv8cfjtfMMmHt0-tS5GDzyKcfaoRru_UnUnDGLIbUXIIxP1PT10SsPcH4LCL6Qh3k_D_dUjK0bACqb9fqWdIgCo-s)

Most users on [Reddit](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEBxCJF15WjJZE00fW0KHTBTHs1HI1oLAoSIMrQ3JN1v-yNBT2ZfmQRJAmc1UUkLCi8LmiHTivD25Cinagvp9ai_cwefZKi5l2PhtyUExKEYNytaW66KXA2uNMkMLTu0VYtovvByHY8szwoOuNx53e84z8d4pnb2BxG9YfrzTiBgsVyJAhsyQtKKG0SspwwlLOHJg) agree on supplementing with electrolytes and potassium—such as bananas, electrolyte drinks, or herbal teas—to help reduce post-alcohol bloat.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEBxCJF15WjJZE00fW0KHTBTHs1HI1oLAoSIMrQ3JN1v-yNBT2ZfmQRJAmc1UUkLCi8LmiHTivD25Cinagvp9ai_cwefZKi5l2PhtyUExKEYNytaW66KXA2uNMkMLTu0VYtovvByHY8szwoOuNx53e84z8d4pnb2BxG9YfrzTiBgsVyJAhsyQtKKG0SspwwlLOHJg)

### What to Avoid While Recovering

- **More alcohol:** Alcohol irritates the stomach lining, increases stomach acid, and disrupts digestion.
- **Salty and greasy foods:** High-sodium snacks and heavy fried foods worsen water retention and slow stomach emptying.
- **Carbonated drinks:** Fizzy beverages and beer add gas directly to the digestive tract.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXjBiVYQK0-L7SfHRFtvJo0XYEKHN5ToRsxJEsgNCt0ksS944EVYxiJsdIYE70aWzNstk5NRRcQAzUDxkqpQffgWZ-zGgkregGHMTcDIlpObtOQ53HQdOuML_TJDZ8l18SwdlWEdeqQo8Qdvb9llDw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF1zDRvHoBHQnZcjOQy3wh0z1mLCsks0rJeOFrAi4YnMm6jgunxp_XBQQQXaDmHQeBB-X9n85vM932Y3HLOcKbbNwXHkgiWLN00S0PWpbWYTJUM9mkH94BIkWA1LU2LkG7-q31pGOYComi4BzOmi81Cr8Dhwie19fZOC9VLdHyEjS0sAHd)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEBxCJF192lTMBxP4_BMx7jI7bzaij4dUDZ9q_BPQ1Zsdncjn6HgynIK8Ci9EH55vz4r2ZXwP3bRzP5gT2hTmyzXgPea9VBJiqfW_YrD_VvBDNqMf74S30mhLl7DmOmi-qj8VP2YhCji2oXuComBxTmoL0d5SMVjDjlrzYy6wioyovSkKF92oLEaKhJCukB-3xRfA)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1_HEBAcI_T82Vm7Fe3U8nltvZiJhs3JX0ARhoorNGW5O5wQ7yNUwdQ4yHl41pt5C9dL0auli7euA_cjDt7O_v5ylsVTZ3AsKIKCv8cfjtfMMmHt0-tS5GDzyKcfaoRru_UnUnDGLIbUXIIxP1PT10SsPcH4LCL6Qh3k_D_dUjK0bACqb9fqWdIgCo-s)

### Preventing Future Bloating & When to See a Doctor
Cutting back on alcohol, pacing drinks with water, eating before drinking, and choosing lower-sugar, non-carbonated drinks can prevent future episodes. You can find more details on causes and prevention at [Healthline](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXsLsUo3NYGsLlummaSgZ4SNjPHstNzddj8GvuvC2fUB1ilMX2gzeX0SBt0y2eppdp3INAMrfNGhkqctTuEc5m8XGpQ4U1txFM25xzsY_cnz8N1nR7zLIx4_z14Z5j--VVSDDy-eN0LV8) and [Addiction Center](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXjBiVYQK0-L7SfHRFtvJo0XYEKHN5ToRsxJEsgNCt0ksS944EVYxiJsdIYE70aWzNstk5NRRcQAzUDxkqpQffgWZ-zGgkregGHMTcDIlpObtOQ53HQdOuML_TJDZ8l18SwdlWEdeqQo8Qdvb9llDw).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF1zDRvHoBHQnZcjOQy3wh0z1mLCsks0rJeOFrAi4YnMm6jgunxp_XBQQQXaDmHQeBB-X9n85vM932Y3HLOcKbbNwXHkgiWLN00S0PWpbWYTJUM9mkH94BIkWA1LU2LkG7-q31pGOYComi4BzOmi81Cr8Dhwie19fZOC9VLdHyEjS0sAHd)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXsLsUo3NYGsLlummaSgZ4SNjPHstNzddj8GvuvC2fUB1ilMX2gzeX0SBt0y2eppdp3INAMrfNGhkqctTuEc5m8XGpQ4U1txFM25xzsY_cnz8N1nR7zLIx4_z14Z5j--VVSDDy-eN0LV8)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXjBiVYQK0-L7SfHRFtvJo0XYEKHN5ToRsxJEsgNCt0ksS944EVYxiJsdIYE70aWzNstk5NRRcQAzUDxkqpQffgWZ-zGgkregGHMTcDIlpObtOQ53HQdOuML_TJDZ8l18SwdlWEdeqQo8Qdvb9llDw)Seek medical care if bloating lasts longer than 72 hours or occurs frequently, or right away if you have severe abdominal pain, fever, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or vomiting blood.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF1_HEBAcI_T82Vm7Fe3U8nltvZiJhs3JX0ARhoorNGW5O5wQ7yNUwdQ4yHl41pt5C9dL0auli7euA_cjDt7O_v5ylsVTZ3AsKIKCv8cfjtfMMmHt0-tS5GDzyKcfaoRru_UnUnDGLIbUXIIxP1PT10SsPcH4LCL6Qh3k_D_dUjK0bACqb9fqWdIgCo-s)Are you trying to relieve **bloating from last night** , or looking for ways to **prevent it** before drinking? references.title: Water
references.text: 1 Drink water If you know you will be having more than just a glass of wine, make sure you drink a lot of water to get rid of alcohol bloating. As mentioned before, alcohol leads to dehydration and drinking water before, during, as well as after drinking can help ease the inflammatory effects alcohol has on your body. And if your bloating is severe and you want to deal with it in an effective and natural way, try Donat. Its unique combination of minerals, which cannot be found in any other mineral water, is clinically proven to aid our digestive system and thus also manage bloating.

references.title: Ginger
references.text: How Ginger Shot Helps Alleviate Bloating: After excessive alcohol consumption, we often wake up with bloating, heartburn, and an upset stomach. This occurs because alcohol produces excess acid and gas in the stomach. However, thanks to the carminative effects of ginger, you can alleviate these symptoms instantly. According to a report by the John Hopkins School of Medicine, ginger contains certain molecules that help manage free radicals, which may react in the body, causing intestinal gas and bloating.

references.title: Antacid
references.text: How to get rid of alcohol bloating A doctor may prescribe medications to protect the stomach lining from damage due to high levels of stomach acid. Examples include Trusted Source : Antacids: These help reduce the harm from stomach acid. Examples include Rolaids and Alka-Seltzer. H2 blockers: These decrease the production of stomach acid and include Pepcid AC. Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs): PPIs, such as Protonix and Nexium, reduce the production of stomach acid. Reducing alcohol consumption can also help manage weight, along with a balanced diet and regular exercise.

references.title: Avocado
references.text: Avocado If you haven't learned from past experiences, you can trust me on this one: don't booze on an empty stomach. Although it'd be ideal to look our best after eating a double cheeseburger, that may not always be the case. However, we need food in order to survive this week of alcoholism. You can beat the bloat by staying away from foods high in carbs and instead try some clean eating. Avocado is not only extremely filling, but also doesn't have enough volume to make you look bloated. Try a side of avocado rather than bread and see the wonders that it'll do for your beach bod.

references.title: Carbonated soft drinks
references.text: Carbonated drinks and alcohol The bubbles in fizzy drinks, sparkling water, beer and sparkling wine are made of gas, which can get trapped in your stomach and cause bloating. Alcohol can be inflammatory and disrupt digestion, leading to bloating, and beer in particular contains both gas and fermentable carbohydrates that can contribute to bloating. Limiting your alcohol intake and drinking plenty of water can help. A woman pours ice-cold cola into glasses.

references.title: Asparagus
references.text: Chow down on some asparagus. Recent research suggests that asparagus helps alleviate hangover symptoms, likely due to its amino acids and minerals, which lessen the toxicity of alcohol on liver cells. Plus, it's a diuretic, so it'll make you pee and get some of that alcohol out of your system. Another green veggie, the artichoke, could also help: Research suggests it tempers the bloating and nausea that come with hangovers.
